home.title: Frequently asked questions about Swishtag
home.description: The simple answers to the questions promotional products companies usually ask before working with Swishtag.

items.question: What is a promotional products technology company?
items.answer: A promotional products technology partner is a software and ecommerce company that understands promo workflows such as PromoStandards data, company stores, artwork approvals and purchase orders, and builds or connects the systems around them. Swishtag does this for distributors, suppliers and decorators.

items.question: Is Swishtag a Shopify development agency or a software company?
items.answer: Both, with a clear distinction. Company Store, Enterprise Automation and PunchOut are solution paths where Swishtag acts as your promotional products technology partner. Promo Plus, Xecutor and Rocket Apps are Swishtag-owned software platforms.

items.question: What is the difference between Solutions and Enterprise Commerce?
items.answer: Solutions focus on launching or improving customer-facing stores. Enterprise Commerce connects the more complex work behind those stores, including suppliers, procurement, ERP, accounting, multi-store management and automation.

items.question: Do we need to replace commonsku, ESP+ or our ERP?
items.answer: No. Swishtag is designed to add a modern commerce and automation layer around the systems your team already trusts. We focus on connecting the gaps rather than forcing a rip and replace project.

items.question: What is PunchOut for promotional products distributors?
items.answer: PunchOut Solutions helps promotional products distributors launch and manage PunchOut catalog connections using Shopify. It can support multiple buyer connections on one Shopify store or connections across multiple Shopify stores from one management platform.

items.question: How much does a Shopify company store cost?
items.answer: The first Shopify company store is $1,200 one-time, additional template stores are $300 each, and Care + Rocket Apps is $100 a month per store. Enterprise automation, PunchOut and custom software are quoted on scope.

items.question: Can you migrate existing company stores to Shopify?
items.answer: Yes. Swishtag can migrate products, customers, content, workflows, and store rules from legacy, custom, WooCommerce, Magento, BigCommerce, and other commerce environments.

items.question: Who is Swishtag built for?
items.answer: Swishtag is a promo tech company focused on promotional products distributors, suppliers and decorators. The strongest fit is an organization trying to launch more programs, connect existing systems or scale without adding the same amount of manual work.

solutions.title: A few things people ask before choosing.
solutions.description: The individual solution pages go deeper. These are the questions that matter when deciding where to start.

items.question: Which solution should we start with?
items.answer: If the immediate goal is one client-facing store, start with Company Store Launch. If you are managing many stores and operational handoffs are the problem, look at Enterprise Automation. If the workflow does not fit an existing package, start with Custom Software & Automation.

items.question: Can we start with Company Store Launch and add automation later?
items.answer: Yes. That is often the cleanest path. Launch the client program first, then add catalog connections, order automation, supplier workflows, PunchOut, accounting, or multi-store controls only when the operation has a real reason for them.

items.question: Can Enterprise Automation manage several Shopify company stores?
items.answer: Yes. That is the core use case. It is designed for distributors that need centralized visibility across multiple Shopify company stores and want to add automation around orders, suppliers, reporting, procurement, or other operational workflows.

items.question: Can Swishtag connect PunchOut, suppliers, or accounting systems?
items.answer: Those integrations belong in the Enterprise Automation scope. The exact connection depends on the systems involved, available APIs, access, and the agreed workflow. PromoStandards can also be part of the broader architecture where appropriate.

items.question: Do we need the enterprise solution just because our company-store business is growing?
items.answer: No. Growth alone is not a reason to add enterprise complexity. Move to the enterprise layer when multiple stores, manual handoffs, reporting, procurement, supplier routing, or custom workflows are creating enough operational drag to justify centralization and automation.

companyStore.title: A few good questions.
companyStore.description: Bring your client program to the demo. We’ll help you define the right starting point.

items.question: What is paid separately?
items.answer: Your Shopify subscription, merchandise, production, fulfillment and shipping are separate. Any paid Shopify add-on app is an extra charge according to that app’s selected pricing plan on Shopify. Your $100/month Care Plan covers the agreed Rocket Apps package and routine store support.

items.question: What do you build for us?
items.answer: A client-branded Shopify company store: storefront design, agreed product and mockup setup, payments, shipping and launch checks. You manage the client relationship, merchandise pricing and fulfillment.

items.question: What is included with an additional store?
items.answer: The $300 setup clones your approved template for another location or program. Each store has its own $100/month Care Plan with the agreed Rocket Apps package. New branding, custom layouts and fresh catalog work are scoped separately; a differently branded store is a $1,200 build.

items.question: Can the store support personalization and employee programs?
items.answer: We configure product options, approved branding and the agreed ordering tools around your program. Employee access, allowances, bulk orders, approvals and other app-dependent features are confirmed in the proposal. Custom workflows are scoped separately.

items.question: Can we use our own suppliers and fulfillment?
items.answer: Yes. We plan the store around print on demand, stocked inventory, preorders or a hybrid approach. Merchandise sourcing and fulfillment remain yours. Supplier connections and automated order routing require a separate scope.

items.question: What happens if we cancel Care?
items.answer: You keep your Shopify account, store and data. Care services and subscription-based Rocket Apps access end. Features that depend on those apps may stop working. Shopify and other app subscriptions remain separate.

items.question: Can you migrate our existing store?
items.answer: Yes. Standard migration can cover up to 250 products, 1,000 customer accounts, 12 months of read-only order history and 100 redirects, subject to a source-data review. Imported records are separate from the 50 newly prepared products and mockups.

items.question: What do you need to get started?
items.answer: Your approved logo, product list, pricing, images, shipping requirements and Shopify access. We confirm the scope and fulfillment approach before work starts. Timelines begin after the deposit and complete content are received.

enterprise.title: Shopify multi-store management FAQs: what distributors usually want to know first
enterprise.description: Start with the platform. Add the complexity only when it solves a real operational problem.

items.question: What is Swishtag’s Shopify company store management platform?
items.answer: Swishtag’s base platform is Shopify multi-store management built for promotional products distributors. It gives your team one place to see and manage multiple Shopify company stores, including centralized order visibility, store-level reporting, portfolio reporting and operational status. You can use it without buying workflow automation.

items.question: What is the difference between the base platform and the add-ons?
items.answer: The base platform covers centralized orders, reporting, store visibility and exceptions. The add-ons, including order routing, supplier connections, PromoStandards, PunchOut, accounting, AI and custom automation, are optional and scoped to your needs.

items.question: Can the platform manage different Shopify company store setups together?
items.answer: Yes. The platform gives you one operational view across Shopify company stores, while each store keeps the setup it needs.

items.question: Which promotional products data systems do you connect with?
items.answer: PromoStandards-supported suppliers, with mapped product data and pricing or inventory where supported. The exact scope depends on API access and your setup.

items.question: Can you connect directly with our approved suppliers?
items.answer: Where an approved supplier provides suitable APIs or technical access, yes. We can automate product data, order submission and status updates, and we confirm what is practical before scoping.

items.question: How does Shopify order routing and workflow automation work?
items.answer: Orders from your stores arrive in one place. Your routing rules split them by supplier, create purchase orders, route work to the right decorator and flag exceptions. It works as a Shopify multi-store order management system layer on top of the base platform.

items.question: Can PunchOut be added later?
items.answer: Yes. PunchOut is an optional add-on, so you can start with the base platform and add it when a client program requires it.

items.question: Can you build enterprise company store automation around our own workflow?
items.answer: Yes. If your distributor operation has a workflow that does not fit an off-the-shelf app, we can map the process and build a custom automation layer where the required systems provide suitable technical access.

items.question: Can you integrate QuickBooks, Sage Intacct, or NetSuite?
items.answer: Yes, these can be scoped as paid finance or ERP integration add-ons, subject to API access, account permissions, required data mappings, licensing, and technical review. We can also assess other accounting or ERP platforms when a practical integration path is available.

items.question: Can you build AI features or connect OpenAI?
items.answer: Yes. Custom add-ons can include OpenAI-powered workflows, customer chatbots, AI calling agents, recommendation engines, internal assistants, and other automation ideas. The final scope depends on the business workflow, data access, privacy requirements, and available APIs.

customSoftware.title: Ask anything about our custom software development services
customSoftware.description: Start with the business problem. We will help turn it into requirements, phases and a practical development path.

items.question: What is included in a custom software project?
items.answer: Our custom software development services cover discovery, requirements and a Solution Blueprint, UX and engineering, integrations and automation, QA and UAT, deployment, documentation, training and handover. You stay involved in business decisions, and Swishtag manages the technical work.

items.question: Do I need a technical specification first?
items.answer: No. You need a clear problem. We turn the business goal into a structured requirement document, phases, assumptions, dependencies and acceptance criteria before development starts.

items.question: Can you work with an existing platform or MVP?
items.answer: Yes. We can build around your existing platform or extend an existing MVP, starting with a review of what is built and where it falls short. For new products, our MVP development approach builds the smallest complete version first.

items.question: Will you give a fixed timeline and price immediately?
items.answer: Not before we understand the problem. After discovery and the Solution Blueprint, you receive phases, a timeline and an investment estimate. Larger or unclear projects may begin with a dedicated blueprint before pricing is finalized.

items.question: Do you use AI in every project?
items.answer: No. We use AI only where it earns its place, such as document processing, data extraction, classification or decision support. Many projects need none. Our AI workflow automation services are scoped around a measurable benefit.

items.question: How do project updates work?
items.answer: Weekly progress updates plus milestone reviews cover completed work, current work, next decisions, blockers and timeline health. We agree on the reporting rhythm before development starts.

items.question: What happens after launch?
items.answer: We deploy to production, stabilize the system and hand over documentation, access, training and an ownership package. The exact package depends on the project.

items.question: Can you integrate with our ERP, accounting or ecommerce platform?
items.answer: Yes. Our API integration services connect ecommerce with ERP, CRM, accounting, supplier and payment systems through APIs, webhooks or middleware. Each project starts by confirming the API access and permissions available for every system involved.

items.question: Can you automate a process without building new software?
items.answer: Yes, where the tools you already use support it. Our business automation services connect them with workflows, and we recommend new software only when existing tools cannot do the job.

items.question: Do you build Shopify apps?
items.answer: Yes. Swishtag has built 100+ custom Shopify applications. Custom Shopify app development covers everything from small tools to multi-store systems. For ready-made apps, see Rocket Apps.

punchout.title: PunchOut Solutions FAQs: Common Questions From Suppliers
punchout.description: A practical overview for suppliers evaluating a procurement-to-ecommerce connection.

items.question: What is a PunchOut catalog?
items.answer: A PunchOut catalog is the buyer-facing part of a wider PunchOut solution. It connects a procurement application with a supplier’s online catalog. The buyer enters the catalog from procurement, selects products, and sends the cart back to the purchasing system to continue the organization’s internal process.

items.question: Which procurement systems can Swishtag work with?
items.answer: Swishtag works with major e-procurement platforms including Coupa, SAP Ariba, JAGGAER, Oracle Procurement and Workday. Support depends on the buyer’s specification.

items.question: Which PunchOut protocols do you support?
items.answer: We support cXML and OCI, the two standard protocols used for B2B PunchOut catalog integration.

items.question: Can approved purchase orders create ecommerce orders automatically?
items.answer: Where the buyer workflow includes electronic purchase orders, Swishtag can map the supported PO data into your ecommerce or order-processing workflow, for example creating a Shopify order from an approved PO.

items.question: Do we have to replace Shopify or our current commerce system?
items.answer: No. We keep your existing B2B ecommerce catalog and add the procurement connection around it.

items.question: Can you support multiple enterprise buyers and stores?
items.answer: Yes. Each buyer is configured and tested against its own requirements, including multi-store and buyer-specific catalog setups.

rocketApps.title: Shopify apps for promotional products: your questions answered
rocketApps.description: Answers to common questions about Rocket Apps and Shopify apps for promotional products stores.

items.question: Do Rocket Apps work with promotional products stores?
items.answer: Yes. Rocket Apps are built by Swishtag, which works with promotional products distributors, suppliers and decorators. They add focused features such as quote requests, forms and gift cards to a Shopify store.

items.question: How do I install a Rocket App?
items.answer: Each app installs from the Shopify App Store. Pick the app, click install and follow the setup steps in your Shopify admin.

items.question: Can I use Rocket Apps on a company store?
items.answer: Yes, they work on Shopify stores, including company stores. See our Shopify company store setup.

items.question: Which Rocket App should I start with?
items.answer: Start with the job that costs you the most time. Quote My Order is for quote requests, Form Builder for custom data, and Address Validator for delivery errors.

items.question: Do I need to replace my platform or ERP?
items.answer: No. Rocket Apps add to your existing Shopify store. For integrations with systems like commonsku or ESP+, see our Solutions page.

items.question: What is the difference between Rocket Apps and Swishtag Solutions?
items.answer: Rocket Apps are focused Shopify apps you install yourself. Solutions are larger projects, such as company store launches and PunchOut, delivered by the Swishtag team.

items.question: Are Rocket Apps free?
items.answer: Several apps are free or have a free plan. Paid apps start at $3.50/month. See each listing for current pricing.

xecutor.title: Manufacturing execution system (MES) software: your questions answered
xecutor.description: Simple answers to the questions decorator and production teams usually ask before bringing Xecutor onto the floor.

items.question: What is Xecutor manufacturing execution system software?
items.answer: Xecutor is Swishtag's manufacturing execution platform for decorator and print-on-demand production. It connects orders, artwork, workflows, workstations, quality and fulfillment in one operational system.

items.question: Can different products follow different production workflows?
items.answer: Yes. Workflows can be built around the production path required by the product, including different workstations and stages for methods such as embroidery, screen printing, heat press and other decorator processes.

items.question: How do operators use Xecutor on the production floor?
items.answer: Operators select their workstation, scan the batch QR code, see the job details and instructions, then complete the assigned work so the job can move to the next stage.

items.question: Can clients connect Shopify or WooCommerce?
items.answer: The current Xecutor setup guide includes Shopify app and WooCommerce plugin connectivity for client store setup and order synchronization.

items.question: Which systems does Xecutor’s MES integration support?
items.answer: The current setup flow includes Dropbox, Stripe, Mailgun and ShipStation on the administration side, plus Shopify and WooCommerce for connected client stores.

items.question: Can Xecutor be adapted to our factory workflow?
items.answer: Yes. The platform is built around configurable workstations, workflows, product settings, team roles and client setup so the production structure can match the operation.

distributors.title: Promotional products distributor FAQs: before you change the stack
distributors.description: Most promotional products distributors do not need a full platform replacement. Start with the client requirement, the existing workflow and the repeated work worth removing.

items.question: Do we need to replace commonsku, ESP+ or our current workflow?
items.answer: No. The goal is not to replace a system that is already working. Our promotional products distributor solutions use Shopify as the customer-facing commerce layer and connect your existing systems only where integration or automation creates a practical improvement.

items.question: Can you build a Shopify company store around our current supplier relationships?
items.answer: Yes. We build Shopify company stores around your existing suppliers, catalogs and fulfillment models, whether the program uses POD, stocked inventory or both.

items.question: Can supplier product data be used inside Shopify?
items.answer: In many cases, yes. Approved supplier product data such as SKUs, colors and pricing can be reused in Shopify, so your team doesn’t rebuild the same catalog manually. The exact scope depends on your setup.

items.question: How do we manage many stores from one place?
items.answer: Centralized reporting, order routing and automation give your team multi-store visibility, so administration doesn’t grow with every new store.

items.question: Can you support PunchOut catalogs and custom enterprise procurement requirements?
items.answer: Yes, when a specific client program requires it. We add PunchOut connectivity for the client’s procurement system.

items.question: What does Swishtag build for promotional products distributors?
items.answer: Online company stores, supplier product data, PunchOut procurement, multi-store automation and custom software, all built around your suppliers, systems and client programs.

items.question: Which systems does Swishtag integrate with?
items.answer: Shopify connects with accounting, ERP, shipping, tax and procurement systems. The exact scope depends on your setup.

suppliers.title: Promotional products supplier FAQs
suppliers.description: How supplier product data, ecommerce and order integration fit together.

items.question: What are promotional products supplier solutions?
items.answer: Promotional products supplier solutions are the product data, ecommerce and integration tools that help a supplier share accurate product information, pricing and availability with distributors and dealers, and handle orders without manual re-entry. Swishtag’s promotional products supplier solutions are built around your existing systems.

items.question: Do we need to replace our ERP or product data system?
items.answer: No. We keep what already works and integrate only where it removes repeated work.

items.question: Can Swishtag help us share product data with distributors?
items.answer: Yes. We help structure SKUs, variants, imagery, pricing and availability once, so they can be reused across distributor stores, dealer portals and other channels. The exact scope depends on your setup.

items.question: Can you automate order intake and acknowledgements?
items.answer: Where it makes sense, yes. We connect incoming orders to your order system and return acknowledgements and status updates, with exceptions surfaced rather than hidden.

items.question: Can you build a Shopify distributor store or dealer portal for us?
items.answer: Yes. We build Shopify-based distributor stores and dealer portals around your pricing and commercial rules.

items.question: Which systems can Swishtag integrate with?
items.answer: Shopify, ERP, accounting, product data and order systems, depending on your setup. Tell us how data moves today, and we’ll recommend what to connect.

items.question: Where should we start?
items.answer: Start with data ownership: which system owns product data, pricing, availability and order status. We map that with you before any integration begins.

decorators.title: Promotional product decorator FAQs
decorators.description: How artwork approval, production and fulfillment fit together for a decorator.

items.question: What is software for promotional product decorators?
items.answer: Swishtag’s promotional product decorator software connects order intake, artwork approval, production workflow, quality control and fulfillment, so every job carries its approved artwork, details and status from order to shipment.

items.question: Do we need to replace our current systems?
items.answer: No. Swishtag works alongside your business management software, order management software and other systems you already use, instead of forcing everything into one oversized platform.

items.question: How does artwork approval work?
items.answer: Promo Plus, our artwork approval software, keeps artwork versions, customer feedback and approvals attached to the job, so production works from the approved, production-ready file.

items.question: How do operators know what to produce?
items.answer: In Xecutor, operators select their workstation, scan the job’s QR code and see the details they need. When the task is done, the workflow moves forward.

items.question: Is this software for screen printers, embroiderers and DTG shops?
items.answer: Yes. Embroidery, screen print, DTG and DTF, heat press and transfers, and sublimation each follow their own route through the stations.

items.question: Can orders from Shopify or WooCommerce flow into production?
items.answer: Yes. Order information can move from your store into production jobs through integrations. The exact scope depends on your setup.

items.question: What is the difference between Promo Plus and Xecutor?
items.answer: Promo Plus manages artwork proofs and customer approval. Xecutor runs the production floor, from workstation tasks to quality control and fulfillment. Together they connect artwork approval to production.

promoPlus.title: Promo Plus FAQs: artwork proofing and approval
promoPlus.description: Answers to common questions about artwork proofing, approval and production files in Promo Plus.

items.question: What does Promo Plus do?
items.answer: Promo Plus is artwork approval software for promotional products. It lets teams build product mockups, send them to clients for approval, track revisions and generate a production-ready proof.

items.question: What is the difference between artwork proofing and artwork approval?
items.answer: Proofing is creating the mockup and the final proof. Approval is the client’s sign-off on it. Promo Plus covers both in one workflow, so the approved version is the one production receives.

items.question: Is Promo Plus artwork approval workflow software or artwork management software?
items.answer: It is built for approval. Promo Plus keeps the artwork, versions, comments and approvals for each project together, but it is not a general file library.

items.question: How do clients review and approve artwork?
items.answer: Share a review link with the customer. They open the current mockup, add comments, ask for changes or approve it, and every response is recorded against the project.

items.question: What does the production team receive?
items.answer: A production-ready PDF with a product proof (item, decoration, imprint size and colors) and an artwork inspection sheet, based on the approved version.

items.question: Who is Promo Plus for?
items.answer: Promotional products distributors, decorators and suppliers, including the sales, design and production teams that handle customer artwork.

items.question: Where can I try it and see pricing?
items.answer: Promo Plus runs on its own site, PromoPlus.io, where you can start a free trial and see current pricing.
